newsitem.title: CHINA: China burns heroin at statue of anti-drugs hero.
newsitem.headline: China burns heroin at statue of anti-drugs hero.

text.p: Chinese authorities on Wednesday burnt a haul of drugs at the foot of a statue of a 19th century anti-drugs hero whose battle against the British opium trade led to the loss of Hong Kong in the "Opium Wars".

Officials in Fuzhou, capital of southeastern Fujian province, burnt 21 kg (46 lb) of heroin and 210 kg (460 lb) of "ice" in front of a sculpture of Lin Zexu, who burnt opium confiscated from British traders 155 years ago thus sparking the first Opium War, the Xinhua news agency said.

China resumes sovereignty over Hong Kong at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule and has sung the praises of Lin Zexu, whose hometown was Fuzhou, for his efforts to stop Britain's opium trade.

In Yili in the westernmost region of Xinjiang, a museum in memory of Lin was opened on Tuesday, Xinhua said. Lin was banished to a remote post in the border region after his destruction of the opium prompted a British armada to blockade several Chinese ports and eventually resulted in the loss of Hong Kong.
The drugs haul occurred during a nationwide crackdown on illegal drugs.
